name: Uzbekistan
summary_text: Uzbekistan is dangerous for trans visitors. Article 120 of the Criminal Code criminalises male same-sex conduct (up to 3 years) — and Human Dignity Trust notes transgender people may be targeted under it, since there is no legal gender recognition and trans people are legally their birth sex. There is substantial evidence of recent enforcement: frequent arrests, and extortion by threat of arrest, with police as the most common perpetrators of anti-LGBT violence; torture goes unpunished (HRW). Because of criminalisation, victims cannot report violence to authorities. ECOM's 2024 national report documents continuing rights violations, and the Justice Ministry denies registration to independent human-rights groups — no community infrastructure can operate openly. There is no documented trans-visitor case, but the legal mechanism (birth-sex status + Art 120) means a trans visitor discovered in a same-sex-appearing relationship faces direct prosecution risk, and discovery itself invites extortion.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Uzbekistan's criminalisation of same-sex activity (Article 120 of the criminal code, up to 3 years).

sources.title: World Report 2024: Uzbekistan | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW World Report 2024 Uzbekistan chapter: includes a Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity section amid a deteriorating human-rights record (harassment of bloggers, Karakalpakstan impunity, constitutional changes).

ECOM national report (2024) on violations of the rights of LGBT people in Uzbekistan: legislation, anti-discrimination legislation, criminalisation of HIV transmission, legal gender recognition, access to human rights, right to health and right to work.

sources.title: Uzbekistan - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2021 Human Rights Report for Uzbekistan: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under Article 120; police abuse and societal stigma; no legal protections.

sources.title: Uzbekistan - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Uzbekistan: official assessment - continued criminalisation under Article 120, societal discrimination, and no anti-discrimination protections.

sources.title: Uzbekistan: Gay Men Face Abuse, Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (March 2021): 'Uzbekistan: Gay Men Face Abuse in Prison' - documents the abuse, extortion and violence gay men face in prison under Article 120 prosecutions.
